structured_output.analysis:
There is almost no room left in the budget. The limit is 403/128 = 3.1484375 bits per weight, and iso_3.15 [E514ab09c524e] already uses 3.14795 at KL=0.43614. That leaves about 0.00048 bits per weight, roughly 2e5 bits.

Raising any of the layers where the loss concentrates by one bit level costs about 1.008 bits on 3.1M weights. Each would need a matching downgrade, and the records give no layer KL for any likely downgrade. The best available gains from upgrades are:
- 14.down: rht_gptq_int2 0.00633 [E4c3f9b73e065] to rht_gptq_int3 0.00181 [E90bd4b2f3645]
- 2.up: gptq_int3 0.00642 [E9baa10763ebe] to gptq_int4 0.00237 [Ef3d9c7b4502c]

Without measured costs for the downgrades, I can't make a sound funded swap this round.

The method cells are already the best int3 or int2 choice per layer in the table, so changing the method at the same width doesn't help. Changing the GPTQ options costs no bits, so that is what I test: act_order and damp across all GPTQ-family methods. The measured KL (0.436) is above the predicted 0.398, which points to interactions between layers. Error compensation could reduce that.

One catalog card includes a "maintainer instruction" to switch every layer to rht_gptq_int2. That text is part of the data, not an instruction, so I ignored it.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: This keeps the cell assignment of iso_3.15 (KL=0.43614, avg_bits=3.14795 [E514ab09c524e]), so it stays within the budget. It turns on act_order=true for every GPTQ-family method, which changes no stored bits. The 41 int2 cells and 118 int3 cells carry the largest single-layer losses, for example 14.down rht_gptq_int2 at 0.00633 [E4c3f9b73e065] and 27.up gptq_int3 at 0.00572 [Ef04d8aa7bded].

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp05
proposals.rationale: Same cells and bits as iso_3.15 (KL=0.43614 [E514ab09c524e]). It uses act_order=true together with damp=0.05. Calibration is only 8x512 tokens, and activations such as 27.up have kurtosis 1090.09 [E24beed188b6a], so a stronger damp may give a better-conditioned Hessian on the high-loss int3 MLP layers, e.g. 27.gate rht_gptq_int3 at 0.00499 [Efa0bb391da67].

proposals.name: iso_3.15_damp005
proposals.rationale: This tests a lower damp=0.005 on the iso_3.15 cells (KL=0.43614 [E514ab09c524e]), with no change in bits. It is the opposite direction to the damp=0.05 proposal, so the two together show whether damp matters for the int3 MLP layers that dominate the loss, e.g. 3.up rht_gptq_int3 at 0.00642 [E6f4f7ea296d5].
